nodes.body: Audrey's four dogs love running and playing fetch, and they also go crazy for frisbee. On 2023-07-03 she said 'They love running and playing fetch, you should see them sometimes' and shared a photo of two dogs running in a field with a ball in their mouth. On 2023-10-13 she added 'My dogs go crazy for Fetch and Frisbee, and they love to run around and meet other pups. They could keep running for hours!' nodes.header: Audrey loves cooking and finds it therapeutic and creative
nodes.body: Audrey loves cooking. She told Andrew 'I love trying out new recipes and experimenting in the kitchen - it's like an escape for me. It's great for de-stressing and letting my creativity flow.' She also called it 'a form of self-care' and 'so therapeutic.' Cooking is one of her primary ways to relax and express creativity.

nodes.body: Audrey's favorite recipe is Chicken Pot Pie. She described it as 'so cozy and delicious, especially on a cold day.' It is her family's recipe that has 'been around for years.' She said 'The flavors always remind me of my grandma's kitchen - makes me think of all the conversations we used to have at the table.' She offered to share the recipe with Andrew on 2023-07-03.

nodes.header: Audrey's go-to cooking ingredient is garlic
nodes.body: Audrey's go-to cooking ingredient is garlic. She said 'Garlic is my go-to ingredient. I love the smell and taste it adds to dishes' on 2023-07-03.

nodes.body: Audrey's favorite dish to make with garlic is Roasted Chicken. She described it as 'based on my love for Mediterranean flavors. It's a tasty dish that's easy to make and loaded with healthy stuff like chicken, garlic, lemon, and herbs. It's my favorite comfort meal!' She offered to share the recipe with Andrew on 2023-07-03 and shared a photo of a pan of chicken and potatoes on a stove.

nodes.body: When cooking, Audrey loves to put on music and pour a glass of wine. She said 'I love throwing on some music, pouring a glass of wine, and just going with the flow in the kitchen. It's so therapeutic' on 2023-07-03.

nodes.header: Andrew is searching for a dog-friendly rental and struggling to find one (mid-2023)
nodes.body: As of 2023-07-08, Andrew is still searching for a dog-friendly rental and has been unable to find one. He told Audrey on 2023-07-03 'Still can't seem to find any dog-friendly spots to rent. That's a bummer.' On 2023-07-08 he confirmed he wants a dog but: 'I wish I could get one, but like I said, it's tough to find a place and find the right dog.' So his blockers are TWO things: (1) finding a dog-friendly rental, and (2) finding the right dog. He has scouted some on-leash parks but finds them not satisfying — he wants open off-leash areas. Andrew currently has no pets. Audrey responded sympathetically: 'Aw, sorry about the search for dog-friendly spots.'

nodes.body: Andrew has a puppy named Toby. He got Toby around or shortly before 2023-07-11, despite city living. He's a bundle of joy and I couldn't resist taking him home, city living and all.' Toby is bringing him 'a lot of joy.' Andrew sees Toby as a future hiking buddy: 'I should take him hiking with me, they would be great hiking buddies, so smart and loyal.' He shared photos of Toby (a dog sitting on a leash in a room; a dog sitting on a rock in the woods; a dog sitting on a trail with a view of a city).

nodes.header: Andrew has been stressed with work piling up; outdoor activities have taken a backseat (mid-2023 through Oct 2023)
nodes.body: Andrew has been stressed with work for months. As of 2023-07-11, he told Audrey 'Since we last talked, work has been piling up and I've been stuck inside. I miss the peace and feeling of freedom that comes with going for a hike.' Audrey responded 'Yeah you're really stressed then! When work's non-stop, it's hard to get outdoors.' Andrew said work has been stressful 'lately' and he needs a break. By 2023-09-06, this stress is still ongoing. He told Audrey: 'Work's been tough and stressful, so my outdoor activities have taken a backseat. Finding balance has been challenging.' He's compensating with small daily self-care: morning coffee and lunchtime walks. By 2023-10-04, the pattern continues — he told Audrey 'Used to hike a lot, but it's more challenging now with my work life balance' and 'Exploring nature was my escape - a way to find peace. But with my job and living here, it's been harder to get that feeling back. I feel a void in my heart.'

Procedure for calming a dog after a frightening or stressful incident, based on Audrey's response after one of her dogs broke her leash and bolted at the park (2023-09-22). nodes.header: Choosing a Dog That Fits Your Living Space and Lifestyle Procedure
nodes.body: Stage 1 — Draft. Procedure for selecting an appropriate dog based on living situation and activity level, based on Andrew's reflections during his first-dog adoption search (May 2023). nodes.header: Pitfalls: Choosing a Dog That Fits Your Living Space and Lifestyle Procedure
Steps: Assess your living space (size, type — apartment vs house, outdoor access)
nodes.body: Before choosing a dog, evaluate your living space — size, whether it's an apartment or house, and access to outdoor areas. Andrew's framing on 2023-05-06: 'the size of living space ... [is] important.' For Andrew, his apartment situation was a key constraint.

nodes.header: Steps: Match dog size to your living space (smaller dog for apartments)
nodes.body: Once living space is assessed, choose a dog of an appropriate size. Smaller dogs suit apartments; larger dogs need more room. Andrew's example on 2023-05-06: 'For me, a person living in an apartment, a smaller dog would be best.' Size mismatch can lead to a dog with insufficient space to be comfortable.

nodes.header: Steps: Assess your own activity level and energy
nodes.body: Honestly evaluate how active you are — daily walks, runs, time available for dog exercise. Andrew's framing on 2023-05-06: 'the exercise needs of the breed are important' — implying you must first understand your own activity level before matching a breed.

nodes.header: Steps: Match dog's energy and exercise needs to your lifestyle (active person → high-energy dog)
nodes.body: Choose a dog whose exercise needs match your activity level. Andrew's example on 2023-05-06: 'if one is active, consider getting one that loves to play and run.' Mismatch leads to either an under-exercised dog (with behavior issues) or an over-burdened owner. Active people pair with playful/runner breeds; lower-energy owners should consider mellower breeds.
